Y1.description: What young people learn and how they progress through school: demonstrated learning by subject, the behaviors and beliefs that shape learning, and school and postsecondary status. All academic outcomes live here, in three categories.

Y2.description: How young people experience learning and activities: enjoyment, curiosity, lasting interest, seeing relevance, creative expression, and choosing to take part.

Y3.description: The relationships around a young person: belonging, supportive adults, friends, family, and wider networks.

Y4.description: Social and emotional skills: what young people can do, organized by CASEL's five competencies. Beliefs about oneself are in Identity, Confidence & Agency.

Y5.description: Who young people believe they are and what they believe they can do: identity, confidence, purpose and agency.

Y6.description: How young people relate to their community and its systems: values, civic knowledge, critical consciousness, civic action, environmental stewardship and digital citizenship.

Y7.description: Readiness for and results in work and independent adult life: career exploration, transition steps, work skills, credentials, employment, money skills and daily living skills.

Y8.description: A young person's own health and safety: daily health habits, motor skills, health knowledge, sexual health and health care; mental health; felt safety, risk behavior and justice involvement.

F1.description: Caregivers and other adult participants: parenting and home learning, caregiver well-being and connections, adult education and system navigation, and the family's partnership with the program.

F2.description: The material stability of a household or of a young person living independently: income and benefits, food, housing.

A1.description: The adults who serve young people: what they learn, what they change in practice, and whether the workforce is stable and well.

A2.description: The program itself: quality, satisfaction, access and inclusion, reach and dosage (outputs), and systems for engaging families.

A3.description: Change beyond one program: policy and institutions, cross-sector partnerships, and community conditions.

Y1.1.definition: A demonstrated gain in reading (phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension, reading level) or in writing and composition in any genre.
Y1.1.include: Reading level, fluency, comprehension scores; reading or ELA test proficiency; writing quality, essays, published writing presented as a writing skill.
Y1.1.exclude: Confidence or habits about reading or writing; oral presentation; English learners' language acquisition; pre-K pre-literacy.

Y1.2.definition: Growth in English proficiency for English learners (listening, speaking, reading, writing), or maintenance and development of a home language alongside English.
Y1.2.include: ELP level gains, reclassification, WIDA/ELPAC-type scores; bilingual or home-language maintenance for youth.
Y1.2.exclude: A native English speaker learning another language (a world language); adult ESL.

Y1.3.definition: A demonstrated gain in math skill, problem-solving or grade-level math proficiency.
Y1.3.include: Math test scores and proficiency; specific math skills; math used in money contexts when the outcome is the math.
Y1.3.exclude: Math confidence or growth mindset; grades or GPA in a math class; money-management habits.

Y1.4.definition: A demonstrated gain in science (life, physical, earth, environmental), engineering design, or computing and coding, including digital-literacy skills.
Y1.4.include: Science test proficiency; ecosystem or ecology knowledge; engineering design process; coding, computational thinking, digital skills.
Y1.4.exclude: STEM interest; STEM identity; online safety; industry certifications; advanced course enrollment.

Y1.5.definition: A demonstrated gain in history, geography, economics, world languages or another academic subject not covered by Literacy to Science, technology & engineering or Arts learning.
Y1.5.include: History and geography content; economics concepts; a world language learned by a native English speaker; other ESSA well-rounded subjects.
Y1.5.exclude: Civics and government (Civic knowledge); health education (Health knowledge & safety skills); personal finance (Financial capability); practical skills with no academic content.

Y1.6.definition: A demonstrated gain in technique, vocabulary or knowledge of an art form (dance, media arts, music, theatre, visual arts).
Y1.6.include: Instrument proficiency; dance or art vocabulary; juried or assessed artistic skill.
Y1.6.exclude: Creating or performing as self-expression or experience, with no stated skill gain.

Y1.7.definition: Analyzing and evaluating information and sources, research and inquiry skills, and media literacy, in any subject.
Y1.7.include: Evaluating source credibility; identifying misinformation; research projects framed as inquiry skill; analyzing conflicting sources.
Y1.7.exclude: Online privacy and safety; interpersonal problem-solving; analyzing power and injustice.

Y1.8.definition: Early language, literacy, math and cognitive development, and kindergarten readiness, for children below kindergarten age.
Y1.8.include: Pre-literacy (letter recognition, phonemic awareness); early numeracy; readiness assessments; broad developmental milestones on screeners such as the ASQ.
Y1.8.exclude: Early motor skills; developmental screenings received (a service); social-emotional skills of young children.

Y1.9.definition: Observable participation in schoolwork: homework completion, being prepared, class participation.
Y1.9.include: Homework completion rates; asking questions and taking part in class discussions; coming prepared.
Y1.9.exclude: School attendance rates; program attendance; curiosity as a feeling.

Y1.10.definition: Sticking with difficult schoolwork or learning tasks despite setbacks, including task persistence in young children.
Y1.10.include: Persisting on hard problems; not giving up on assignments; early-childhood task persistence.
Y1.10.exclude: General persistence outside learning; frustration tolerance as emotional regulation.

Y1.11.definition: Using specific methods to learn: note-taking, planners, test preparation, self-quizzing, metacognition.
Y1.11.include: Named study techniques; planning schoolwork with a tool.
Y1.11.exclude: General organization outside school; goal-setting in general.

Y1.12.definition: Beliefs about oneself as a learner: academic self-efficacy, belonging in academic work, and growth mindset about intelligence or ability to learn.
Y1.12.include: 'I can succeed in this class'; believing intelligence or math ability grows with effort; confidence in academic abilities.
Y1.12.exclude: General self-confidence; growth mindset about challenges in general.

Y1.13.definition: A student's school attendance, chronic absence, or staying enrolled in school through disruption (homelessness, foster placement changes, pregnancy).
Y1.13.include: Attendance rates for participating students; chronic absenteeism; remaining enrolled or in the school of origin.
Y1.13.exclude: Program attendance or dosage; re-enrolling after dropping out.

Y1.14.definition: Suspensions, expulsions, office discipline referrals, and alternatives that replace them.
Y1.14.include: Fewer suspensions or referrals; restorative alternatives to suspension; school-level suspension rates.
Y1.14.exclude: Reduced fighting or violence; interpersonal conflict resolution skills.

Y1.15.definition: Course grades, GPA, course passing, credit accumulation, promotion, 9th-grade on-track status, and 'academic performance' or test scores with no subject named.
Y1.15.include: GPA; passing core classes; credits for promotion; unspecified academic achievement.
Y1.15.exclude: A test score in a named subject; graduation; attendance.

Y1.16.definition: Enrolling in or completing advanced courses: AP, IB, honors, advanced STEM electives, dual enrollment and college credit earned in high school.
Y1.16.include: AP/IB/honors enrollment; dual enrollment; college credit before graduation.
Y1.16.exclude: Interest in a subject; postsecondary enrollment after high school.

Y1.17.definition: Graduating from high school, earning a GED or equivalency, or re-enrolling after leaving school.
Y1.17.include: On-time graduation; GED; re-engagement after dropout or release.
Y1.17.exclude: Adult GED (caregivers); staying enrolled through disruption.

Y1.18.definition: Enrolling in, persisting in, or completing college or other postsecondary education or training after high school.
Y1.18.include: College enrollment the fall after graduation; first-to-second-year persistence; degree or certificate completion.
Y1.18.exclude: Applications and FAFSA (the process); college credit in high school; combined 'employed or in education' indicators.

Y2.1.definition: A positive emotional experience of the program or of learning: fun, happiness, excitement, pride in being part of it.
Y2.1.include: Reports of enjoying activities; excitement to attend; pride in the program.
Y2.1.exclude: General life satisfaction or flourishing; feeling safe or accepted.

Y2.2.definition: Interest sparked in the moment: curiosity, asking questions about something new, willingness to try a new activity.
Y2.2.include: Asking questions during a demonstration; trying new activities; showing curiosity.
Y2.2.exclude: Interest that lasts or is pursued beyond the program; general confidence to take on challenges.

Y2.3.definition: Interest that persists, deepens or becomes the young person's own: a passion, returning to a topic, pursuing it beyond the program.
Y2.3.include: Discovering a passion; continuing an activity after the program; self-directed pursuit of a topic.
Y2.3.exclude: Momentary curiosity; interest in a career field; identity ('I am a ___ person').

Y2.4.definition: Seeing learning as useful for one's goals, future plans or community.
Y2.4.include: Explaining how a subject connects to careers or daily life; valuing what is learned.
Y2.4.exclude: Career awareness; general purpose in life.

Y2.5.definition: Self-expression through making something (art, music, writing, design), presenting or performing finished work, or responding to art, as an experience rather than a stated skill gain.
Y2.5.include: Composing, creating, exhibiting, performing, critiquing or connecting art to personal meaning.
Y2.5.exclude: A stated technique or knowledge gain in an art form; a stated writing skill gain; teamwork during a production.

Y2.6.definition: An individual young person's choice to take part in constructive activities, inside the program (returning, joining) or outside it (sports, arts, clubs, faith groups).
Y2.6.include: Returning for another year; joining a team or club; participating fully alongside peers; per-person participation thresholds.
Y2.6.exclude: Aggregate program attendance, counts or rates; the program's accommodations.

Y3.1.definition: Feeling accepted, valued, included and safe in the program, school or a community; mattering; less isolation.
Y3.1.include: Sense of belonging; feeling safe and accepted in program spaces; feeling connected to a new community; reduced loneliness.
Y3.1.exclude: Feeling safe in general (home, neighborhood); trauma-related safety; one named trusted adult; named friendships.

Y3.2.definition: A caring, trusting relationship with at least one adult outside the family (mentor, staff, teacher, coach), including its quality (care, challenge, support).
Y3.2.include: Naming a trusted adult; a mentor who cares or challenges; permanent adult connections for youth in care.
Y3.2.exclude: A wider network used to open opportunities; family relationships.

Y3.3.definition: Friendships, peer acceptance and a positive peer group.
Y3.3.include: Making friends; a supportive peer community; friendships across groups.
Y3.3.exclude: The skill of working together; general belonging to the program.

Y3.4.definition: The young person's own relationship with their family: communication, connection, repair, reunification.
Y3.4.include: Reunification; rebuilding trust with family; better communication with parents as described from the youth side.
Y3.4.exclude: Parenting practices (the parent is the subject); housing.

Y3.5.definition: Access to, and use of, a wider network of relationships (adults, peers, professionals, employers) that can open educational or career opportunities.
Y3.5.include: Expanding a professional network; introductions and references; contacts who can help with a goal.

Y4.1.definition: Recognizing and naming one's own emotions.
Y4.1.include: Identifying feelings; using a feelings chart; naming emotions in hard moments.

Y4.2.definition: Managing strong emotions and impulses, and using coping strategies for stress, worry or frustration.
Y4.2.include: Calming down; frustration tolerance; self-regulation; deep breathing or journaling to manage stress.
Y4.2.exclude: Reduced symptoms of anxiety or depression; caregiver stress; academic persistence.

Y4.3.definition: Setting personal goals and working toward them, and general organization, self-discipline and persistence outside schoolwork.
Y4.3.include: Setting and pursuing goals; completing projects; keeping materials organized; follow-through.
Y4.3.exclude: Study techniques; persistence with schoolwork; career plans.

Y4.4.definition: Understanding and caring about others' feelings and perspectives, expressing gratitude, and reading social norms and expectations in different settings.
Y4.4.include: Perspective-taking; compassion; gratitude; understanding expectations in class, online and community settings.
Y4.4.exclude: Respect for people of other backgrounds; listening as a behavior.

Y4.5.definition: Respecting and including people of different backgrounds and identities, and examining one's own biases.
Y4.5.include: Respect for peers of other cultures, religions, abilities; inclusive behavior; bias awareness.
Y4.5.exclude: Pride in one's own identity; friendships across groups.

Y4.6.definition: Expressing oneself clearly, listening actively, and speaking to an audience.
Y4.6.include: Active listening; clear communication; presentations and public speaking.
Y4.6.exclude: Workplace communication; written composition; confidence about speaking in class.

Y4.7.definition: Working with others toward shared goals, including leading peers within a group task.
Y4.7.include: Collaboration on projects; teamwork; taking turns leading a small group; leadership within a team activity.
Y4.7.exclude: Leadership that influences a program, school or community decision; friendships; workplace leadership.

Y4.8.definition: Building, maintaining and repairing relationships, and resolving interpersonal conflict constructively.
Y4.8.include: Resolving disagreements without fighting; de-escalation; repairing a friendship.
Y4.8.exclude: Reduced incidence of fights; exclusionary discipline; the relationship outcome itself.

Y4.9.definition: Knowing where to find support, asking for help, and offering help to others.
Y4.9.include: Willingness to seek help; naming resources to contact in a crisis; helping peers.
Y4.9.exclude: Actually receiving mental health services; self-advocacy for accommodations.

Y4.10.definition: Weighing options and consequences and working a personal or social problem through from identifying it to acting.
Y4.10.include: Pros and cons before a decision; structured problem-solving; anticipating consequences.
Y4.10.exclude: Interpersonal conflict; academic analysis of sources; ethical choices.

Y4.11.definition: Making an ethical or prosocial choice in a specific situation, including small daily contributions to the class or program.
Y4.11.include: Reporting bullying instead of joining in; standing up for a classmate; helping clean up the space.
Y4.11.exclude: General character traits; challenging systems of injustice; organized community service.

Y4.12.definition: Avoiding unsafe situations and resisting negative peer pressure.
Y4.12.include: Refusal skills; leaving unsafe situations; resisting pressure to use substances.
Y4.12.exclude: An actual change in substance use or violence; safety knowledge such as first aid.

Y5.1.definition: Understanding who one is, what matters to one, and how one is changing.
Y5.1.include: Identity exploration; articulating one's values and experiences.
Y5.1.exclude: Pride in a cultural or social identity; self-confidence; purpose.

Y5.2.definition: Pride in, and acceptance of, one's own cultural, ethnic, linguistic, gender, sexual or other social identity.
Y5.2.include: Pride in heritage; self-acceptance of sexual orientation or gender identity; bicultural identity.
Y5.2.exclude: Respect for others' identities; home-language skill.

Y5.3.definition: Seeing oneself as a certain kind of person in a field: 'a STEM person', an artist, an athlete, a reader, a writer.
Y5.3.include: 'See themselves as' statements tied to a field.

Y5.4.definition: A general belief that one can succeed and handle challenges, including general growth mindset and self-esteem.
Y5.4.include: Self-confidence; self-efficacy; self-esteem; naming one's strengths; growth mindset about setbacks.
Y5.4.exclude: Confidence about schoolwork; confidence in a named physical skill where the skill is the outcome.

Y5.5.definition: A sense of purpose and meaning, optimism about the future, and aspirations, including spiritual purpose and growth in faith.
Y5.5.include: Sense of purpose; hopes and goals for life; growth in faith or spiritual life.
Y5.5.exclude: Faith-grounded values (Values & character); belonging to a faith community (Belonging); career aspirations (Career exploration).

Y5.6.definition: Acting as the causal agent in one's own life: making choices, advocating for one's own needs, directing one's own supports.
Y5.6.include: Self-advocacy in IEP meetings; leading one's own IEP; requesting accommodations; making and explaining one's own choices.
Y5.6.exclude: Influencing collective decisions; asking for help in general.

Y6.1.definition: General character traits and guiding values: integrity, honesty, responsibility, sportsmanship, forgiveness, faith-grounded values.
Y6.1.include: Honesty; responsibility; sportsmanship; living out values, including faith-based values.
Y6.1.exclude: A choice in one specific situation; faith growth or spiritual purpose.

Y6.2.definition: Understanding how government, civic institutions, elections and rights work.
Y6.2.include: How a bill becomes law; branches of government; how the school board decides; voter registration process.
Y6.2.exclude: Families learning to navigate school or benefit systems; history content.

Y6.3.definition: Analyzing power, inequity and systems of oppression, and acting against injustice.
Y6.3.include: Analyzing why food deserts or zoning inequality exist; articulating how systemic racism affects a community.
Y6.3.exclude: Standing up for a classmate in one situation; respect for diversity.

Y6.4.definition: Influencing collective decisions and taking part in civic life: youth councils, testimony, advocacy, co-design, organizing, voting, and civic efficacy.
Y6.4.include: Presenting to a city council; youth advisory boards; organizing campaigns; registering and voting; believing one can influence community decisions.
Y6.4.exclude: Leading peers within a group task; one's own IEP or personal choices.

Y6.5.definition: Organized service or projects to improve the community, including identifying a community issue and planning action on it.
Y6.5.include: Service hours; service trips; food drives; community action plans.
Y6.5.exclude: Small daily help in the program; environmental action; civic advocacy aimed at decision-makers.

Y6.6.definition: Caring for the environment and acting on it: pro-environmental behavior and connection to nature.
Y6.6.include: Recycling and composting; reducing waste; stewardship; connection to nature.
Y6.6.exclude: Knowledge of ecosystems; feeling restored in nature.

Y6.7.definition: Safe, legal and ethical behavior online: privacy, security, recognizing scams, respectful conduct.
Y6.7.include: Protecting personal information; strong passwords; recognizing phishing.
Y6.7.exclude: Evaluating news credibility; coding skills; device access.

Y7.1.definition: Learning about careers and pathways, interest inventories, workplace and campus visits, and interest in or aspiration toward a career field.
Y7.1.include: Researching careers; exploring pathways; interest in a STEM career; college visits.
Y7.1.exclude: Applications and FAFSA; lasting interest in an activity.

Y7.2.definition: Knowing and completing the process of moving to college or work: applications, FAFSA, financial aid, resumes, interviews.
Y7.2.include: FAFSA completion; college applications; comparing aid letters; resume writing.
Y7.2.exclude: Enrolment itself; employability behaviors on the job.

Y7.3.definition: Professionalism and workplace skills: punctuality, workplace communication, initiative, job performance.
Y7.3.include: Professional conduct; supervisor evaluations; workplace communication.
Y7.3.exclude: Having or keeping a job; general SEL skills outside a work context.

Y7.4.definition: Industry-specific skills, recognized credentials and certifications, and completing internships or apprenticeships.
Y7.4.include: Industry certifications; apprenticeship completion; trade skills.
Y7.4.exclude: Employment after training; academic computing skills.

Y7.5.definition: Getting or keeping a job, wages and earnings, and combined 'employed or in education' indicators.
Y7.5.include: Job placement; paid work hours; wages; competitive integrated employment; WIOA-style combined indicators.

Y7.6.definition: The young person's own financial knowledge, habits and decisions: budgeting, saving, banking, credit, understanding pay and taxes.
Y7.6.include: Budgets; savings accounts; reading a pay stub; understanding credit and interest.
Y7.6.exclude: Household income or benefits; the youth's wages; arithmetic with money as context.

Y7.7.definition: Daily living skills for self-sufficiency: cooking, scheduling, transportation, self-care away from home, and obtaining vital documents.
Y7.7.include: Independent-living skill bundles; getting an ID, Social Security card and birth certificate; self-care at camp.

Y8.1.definition: Everyday health behaviors: physical activity and fitness, nutrition and healthy eating, sleep, hygiene, and recreational screen time.
Y8.1.include: Minutes of activity; fitness; fruit and vegetable intake; healthy cooking framed as nutrition; hours of sleep; handwashing; less screen time.
Y8.1.exclude: Sport or motor skill gains; health care visits; first aid; household food access.

Y8.2.definition: Fundamental movement, fine and gross motor, and sport-specific or outdoor physical skills.
Y8.2.include: Dribbling and passing; swimming levels; running, jumping, throwing; fine motor skills; hiking or climbing technique.
Y8.2.exclude: Fitness or activity minutes; confidence in general.

Y8.3.definition: Health information and safety skills not covered by another health code: first aid, injury prevention, finding reliable health information, and health education content.
Y8.3.include: First aid; outdoor safety; health class content; how to respond to an allergic reaction.
Y8.3.exclude: Sexual health knowledge; substance-risk knowledge; industry safety credentials.

Y8.4.definition: Knowledge and behavior related to sexual health, STI and pregnancy prevention, and healthy relationships in that context.
Y8.4.include: STI prevention knowledge; delaying pregnancy; accessing confidential services.

Y8.5.definition: Getting and using health care: insurance, preventive and dental or vision visits, screenings, immunizations, and managing chronic conditions.
Y8.5.include: Enrolling in insurance; annual screenings; developmental screenings received; asthma self-management.
Y8.5.exclude: Mental health services; parents keeping infants' well-child visits.

Y8.6.definition: Fewer symptoms of anxiety, depression, distress or behavioral problems in the young person.
Y8.6.include: Lower anxiety or depression scores; fewer outbursts; less self-reported stress.
Y8.6.exclude: Coping skills; caregiver stress; loneliness framed socially.

Y8.7.definition: Positive mental health: life satisfaction, flourishing, feeling restored or well.

Y8.8.definition: A young person processing trauma, feeling psychologically safe during recovery, and moving toward healing.
Y8.8.include: Processing traumatic events; psychological safety for trauma-exposed youth.
Y8.8.exclude: Staff adopting trauma-informed practice; general felt safety.

Y8.9.definition: Being connected to and using counseling, therapy or crisis services.
Y8.9.include: Referrals completed; sessions attended; connection to community providers.
Y8.9.exclude: Knowing where to get help (a skill); staff training on referrals.

Y8.10.definition: Feeling safe at home, at school or in the neighborhood, not specific to the program.
Y8.10.include: Feeling safe walking to school or in the neighborhood.
Y8.10.exclude: Safety and acceptance in the program; trauma-related safety; safe choices; reduced victimization.

Y8.11.definition: Use, intentions or perceived risk of tobacco, vaping, alcohol or other drugs.
Y8.11.include: Reduced use; delayed first use; lower intentions; higher perceived risk; knowledge of risks.

Y8.12.definition: Fighting, weapon carrying, bullying, harassment, dating violence and community violence, as perpetrator or victim.
Y8.12.include: Fewer fights; less weapon carrying; less harassment; dating-violence warning signs.

Y8.13.definition: Avoiding justice-system involvement, completing diversion or probation, and reduced recidivism.
Y8.13.include: No new adjudication; completing a restorative agreement; avoiding re-arrest.
Y8.13.exclude: Re-enrolling in school or getting a job after release.

F1.1.definition: Caregivers' child-development knowledge, parenting practices, parent-child interaction and parenting confidence, including teen parents.
F1.1.include: Knowledge of milestones; positive discipline; positive interactions; parenting confidence.
F1.1.exclude: Home learning routines; family health practices; the youth's side of the relationship.

F1.2.definition: Family practices that support a child's learning and development at home: reading together, routines, homework time.
F1.2.include: Reading at home; bedtime and daily routines; homework space.

F1.3.definition: Caregiver or household health practices for children: breastfeeding, safe sleep, well-child visits kept by the parent, family eating habits.
F1.3.include: Breastfeeding; safe sleep; well-child visits; family fruit and vegetable intake.
F1.3.exclude: Household food access; the youth's own health care.

F1.4.definition: The caregiver's own stress, mental health and resilience.
F1.4.include: Reduced parenting stress; lower caregiver depression; resilience.
F1.4.exclude: The child's mental health; adult learners' tech anxiety about a skill.

F1.5.definition: Caregivers building supportive relationships with other parents or their community.
F1.5.exclude: The family's relationship with the program.

F1.6.definition: The education, training, English proficiency, digital or financial skills, and employment of a caregiver or other adult participant.
F1.6.include: GED or job training for parents; adult ESL; digital literacy for family members or older adults.
F1.6.exclude: Household income; young people's own skills.

F1.7.definition: Families knowing their rights, knowing where to turn for help, navigating school or service systems, and getting connected to resources.
F1.7.include: IDEA rights knowledge; understanding enrollment and health systems; connecting to resources; knowing where to turn in a crisis.
F1.7.exclude: Receiving benefits; civic knowledge of government.

F1.8.definition: The family's relationship with and trust in the program or school, and communication between them.
F1.8.include: Families feeling welcome; trust in staff; feeling connected to the school community.
F1.8.exclude: Parents' confidence in program safety or satisfaction; family participation in events or decisions.

F1.9.definition: Families attending, volunteering or taking part in program or school decisions.
F1.9.include: Serving on advisory councils; attending workshops (per-family thresholds); volunteering.
F1.9.exclude: Aggregate family attendance counts; the organization creating structures.

F2.1.definition: Household or independent-youth income, public benefits, and financial stability.
F2.1.include: Household income; SNAP/TANF/Medicaid enrollment; household savings.
F2.1.exclude: The youth's own money skills; caregiver job training.

F2.2.definition: Having enough food and access to healthy food.
F2.2.include: Reduced food insecurity; fewer skipped meals; less reliance on emergency food.
F2.2.exclude: Household eating practices; food distribution counts.

F2.3.definition: Securing or keeping safe, stable housing, for a household or a young person living independently.
F2.3.include: Exits to stable housing; avoiding eviction; keeping a lease; reduced rent burden.
F2.3.exclude: Services delivered toward housing; school stability.

A1.1.definition: Staff, volunteers, mentors, coaches or case managers gaining knowledge or skills.
A1.1.include: Training outcomes; staff confidence; volunteers' understanding.
A1.1.exclude: Training hours completed (an output); applying the learning.

A1.2.definition: Adults applying new practices, including trauma-informed care.
A1.2.include: Implementing a curriculum or screener; adopting restorative or trauma-informed practice.

A1.3.definition: Staff retention and turnover, and staff well-being.

A2.1.definition: Observed or assessed program quality (safe, supportive, interactive, engaging environment) and accreditation.
A2.1.include: YPQA or similar scores; accreditation; a more welcoming or affirming environment.

A2.2.definition: Participants' or families' satisfaction with the program and their perceptions of its quality and safety.
A2.2.include: Satisfaction ratings; parents' confidence in program safety.
A2.2.exclude: Youth enjoyment; family trust in staff.

A2.3.definition: Providing materials, devices, connectivity or facilities, including counts of resources distributed.
A2.3.include: Laptops and hotspots; home internet; facilities access.

A2.4.definition: Removing barriers so that all participants can take part: accommodations, accessible formats, interpretation and translation.
A2.4.include: Sensory kits and visual schedules; accessible materials; interpreters; home-language communications.
A2.4.exclude: Youth participating alongside peers (their participation); families navigating systems.

A2.5.definition: Program-level counts, rates and dosage: youth served, attendance rates, sessions, match length, training hours, and services staff delivered.
A2.5.include: Number served; average daily attendance; match duration; sessions delivered; applications submitted by staff.
A2.5.exclude: An individual youth's choice to return; a student's school attendance.

A2.6.definition: The organization's systems, events or policies for engaging families.
A2.6.include: Creating a parent advisory council; family engagement policies; family events offered.
A2.6.exclude: Parents serving on the council; interpretation services.

A3.1.definition: Changes to policy, funding or institutional practice in schools, districts, cities or states.
A3.1.include: New ordinances; district policies; dedicated budget funding.
A3.1.exclude: Partnerships and data sharing; program quality.

A3.2.definition: Shared agendas, shared measurement and coordinated partnerships across organizations and sectors.
A3.2.include: Data-sharing agreements; shared data systems; coalition collaboration.

A3.3.definition: Neighborhood cohesion, trust and willingness to act for the common good.
A3.3.include: Residents' trust; willingness to intervene for youth safety.
